header.title: Open Paint Studio
header.proof4: API and MCP for AI assistants
header.heroAlt: Open Paint Studio: a sketched floor plan with rooms, a dimension line and notes in red and green, with the Home ribbon and the history on the right
header.label: Image editing
header.tagline: Make a quick sketch or mark up a screenshot, without a heavy photo editor
header.desc: Open Paint Studio is a lightweight image editor in the spirit of MS Paint. Draw with a brush, shapes and text, crop and rotate in one click, and shapes and text stay editable: move, scale or recolour them afterwards.

meta.description: Free, open-source image editor in the spirit of MS Paint: sketch, mark up and edit images, with shapes and text that stay editable. Opens almost any image format, exports to PNG, JPEG, WebP and SVG. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
meta.title: Open Paint Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

draw.alt: Typing text straight onto the floor plan, with the Apply text button and the font and bold options in the ribbon
draw.title: Sketch and write straight on the canvas
draw.desc: Brush, eraser, fill, eyedropper, lines, rectangles and ellipses, with adjustable size, opacity and a colour palette. Click where you want text and type; pick font, size and bold in the ribbon. The fonts ship with the app, so it works offline too.

vector.alt: Forge dark theme: a text note on the floor plan is selected with a frame and a handle for scaling, with the Object menu in the ribbon
vector.title: Move and restyle what you have already drawn
vector.desc: Shapes and text remain separate objects. Select one to move it, drag the corner to scale, or give it a different colour, size or font. Ctrl+A grabs everything at once, and an SVG export keeps them editable for other programs.

image.alt: A screenshot of a schedule with a red frame, a circle, an arrow and a yellow highlight, with the Image ribbon open
image.title: Mark up a screenshot and pass it on
image.desc: Open a screenshot or photo, add frames, arrows and text, and export to PNG or JPEG. Crop, resize, rotate and flip sit in one ribbon, as do brightness, contrast, saturation, greyscale, invert and sepia.

files.alt: The File menu with open, save and export, and the Supported formats window with a long list of file types
files.title: Opens almost any image, without uploading
files.desc: PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF, but also TIFF, HEIC from your phone, PSD, SVG, JPEG XL and camera RAW. Everything is processed on your own computer; nothing goes to the cloud. Save your work as PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG or IFCX.

ai.alt: Blueprint theme: the Automation ribbon with the API · MCP window for the address, the token and a document ID
ai.title: Let an AI assistant draw along
ai.desc: A local API with its own token and an MCP server let an assistant such as Claude create an image, draw on it and show the result. Ask for a 1200 × 800 sketch with a coloured area, for instance; then load it in the app and carry on yourself.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Draw, mark up and touch up, in one lightweight app
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

brush.title: Brush with smooth strokes
brush.desc: Draw freehand with adjustable size and opacity.

eraser.title: Eraser, fill and eyedropper
eraser.desc: Erase a part, fill an area with colour or pick a colour from the image.

shapes.title: Lines, rectangles and ellipses
shapes.desc: As an outline or filled, in any colour from the palette or the colour picker.

text.title: Text on the canvas
text.desc: Type straight into the image, in sans serif, serif or monospace, and bold if you like.

palette.title: Colour palette and opacity
palette.desc: Pick from the palette in one click or set your own colour, semi-transparent too.

objects.title: Move and scale objects
objects.desc: Select a shape or text, drag it elsewhere or pull the corner.

restyle.title: Restyle afterwards
restyle.desc: Give a drawn object a different colour, size or font, or delete it.

selectall.title: Select everything with Ctrl+A
selectall.desc: Move, scale or delete all objects at once.

svg.title: Editable SVG
svg.desc: Export shapes and text as real SVG objects, to continue in a drawing program.

crop.title: Crop and resize
crop.desc: Drag a frame to crop or enter a new width and height.

rotate.title: Rotate and flip
rotate.desc: A quarter turn left or right, flip horizontally or vertically; shapes and text stay editable.

adjust.title: Colour corrections
adjust.desc: Brightness, contrast and saturation with sliders.

filters.title: Greyscale, invert and sepia
filters.desc: One-click filters; undo puts the shapes back as they were.

open.title: Almost any image format
open.desc: From PNG and JPEG to TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, PSD, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000 and camera RAW.

local.title: Everything on your own computer
local.desc: No upload and no account; even the tricky formats are converted locally.

export.title: Export to PNG, JPEG and WebP
export.desc: Ready to email, put in a report or place on a website.

ifcx.title: IFCX and IFCXB
ifcx.desc: Save the image in the open IFCX format, so other OpenAEC apps can read it.

assoc.title: Double-click to open
assoc.desc: The desktop app associates itself with images and IFCX files.

draft.title: Your draft is kept
draft.desc: Close the window and your drawing is still there next time, with all editable objects.

undo.title: 40 steps back
undo.desc: Undo and redo, with a history that shows every step.

zoom.title: Zoom, pan and grid
zoom.desc: Ctrl+scroll from 10 to 400 percent, drag with the middle mouse button and a pixel grid.

focus.title: Focus mode and shortcuts
focus.desc: Hide the ribbon for more drawing space; B, E, F, I, L, R, O and T pick the tool.

themes.title: Five themes, two languages
themes.desc: Light, Forge, OpenAEC, Blueprint and high contrast, in Dutch and English.

api.title: Local API with a token
api.desc: Send your image to the API or load one from it; a revision check stops you overwriting each other's work.

mcp.title: MCP server for AI assistants
mcp.desc: Six tools: create, list and read documents, draw, undo and show the result as a PNG.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.43.2
whatsnew.title: First release, for every system
whatsnew.desc: The first Open Paint Studio release from the OpenAEC Foundation, with signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux.

files.a: Almost any image: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, PSD, SVG, ICO, TGA, JPEG 2000, JPEG XL, camera RAW and IFCX/IFCXB. For animations and multi-page files the first frame opens.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Yes, the app itself. On Windows it installs for your user, without admin rights; on Linux the AppImage runs without installing. There is no public web version yet.

price.q: What does Open Paint Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The app is free and open source under the MIT licence, with no account or subscription. The OpenAEC house style in the app is under CC BY-SA 4.0.

save.q: In which format is my work saved?
save.a: The app automatically keeps your current drawing as a draft on your own device, with all editable objects. As a file you export to PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG, or save the image in IFCX or IFCXB.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon, one universal DMG) and Linux (.deb and AppImage). The installers are signed.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: Through the MCP server an assistant such as Claude can create images, draw on them, undo a step and show the result as a PNG. You run the API and MCP separately next to the app, from the source code; the installer does not start them for you.

reopen.q: Can I edit shapes and text again later from a file?
reopen.a: Not yet in Open Paint Studio itself. While you work on a drawing the objects stay editable, even after closing the window. IFCX stores the image as a picture; to keep editing the shapes elsewhere, export to SVG.

offline.q: Do I need an internet connection?
offline.a: No. The fonts and the image conversion are built into the app, and your images go nowhere. You only need the internet to download the app.

photo.q: Does it replace a photo editor?
photo.a: No, and it isn't meant to be. There are no layers, masks or selections of part of a photo. Open Paint Studio is for the quick jobs: sketching, marking up, cropping and a colour correction.

tauri.desc: A thin native shell in Rust for Windows, macOS and Linux, with small installers.

react.desc: The editor draws on an HTML canvas; shapes and text are kept as operations.

magick.desc: Reads TIFF, HEIC, PSD, RAW and other formats locally, in a separate worker.

ifcx.desc: The image as a PNG inside an IFCX document; IFCXB is the same content as CBOR with gzip.

mcp.desc: An MCP server on the official TypeScript SDK and an API that only listens on your own computer, with a token and revision checks.

signing.title: Signed releases
signing.desc: Windows installer with a digital signature, macOS app notarized by Apple, Linux packages with an OpenPGP signature and SHA256SUMS.
